newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai brokers re-register B share accounts.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai brokers re-register B share accounts.

text.p: Major brokerages in Shanghai have begun to re-register foreign currency B share accounts to bar domestic investors from trading the shares, which are reserved for foreigners, officials said on Thursday.
The officials said the central securities authorities had ordered brokerages to re-register all B share accounts by March 15.
China's securities rules ban domestic investors from trading B shares, but about half of all trading on the B share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen has been from domestic investors in recent months.
"We have begun to re-register the accounts to bar domestic investors from trading foreign currency B shares," said one official with a major securities house.
"The order is from the China Securities Regulatory Commission and says that all brokerages must finish the registration by March 15," said a second official.
China established the B share markets in 1992 and in the first couple of years, almost all the shares were in the hands of foreign investors.
But a market slump starting in mid-1994 prompted the exchanges and brokerages to quietly open trading to locals, who have since become the dominant players on the market, brokers said.
Beijing has repeatedly re-affirmed the ban but has so far failed to drive domestic investors from the markets, they said.
